title: Biomolecular Imaging of Cellular Uptake of Nanoparticles using Multimodal Nonlinear Optical Microscopy
protocol: Switch on the interlock system.
Select arm laser before starting the system.
Turn on the PC with the software to control the dual-output femtosecond laser.
Load the software for the dual-output femtosecond laser.
Hold down on the Power icon for a count of 3 to switch on the laser emission.
Wait until the laser has warmed up and the laser-ready light is lit green in the software.
Select 802 nm as the wavelength of the pump beam through the software.
Open the shutters of the tunable pump beam by holding down on the aperture images for 3 s.
Open the shutters of the 1,045 nm Stokes beam by holding down on the aperture images for 3 s.
Switch on the Spectral Focusing Timing and Recombination Unit (SF-TRU).
Load ATM software on the same PC as the laser software.
Control the delay stages and laser attenuators with the ATM software.
Ensure pump beam polarization is vertical.
Ensure Stokes beam polarization is vertical.
Independently control polarizations of both beams using half-wave plates.
Attenuate pump beam to less than 10%.
Attenuate Stokes beam to less than 15%.
Set optimal laser settings for cellular imaging: 6% (pump) and 10% (Stokes).
Corresponding power levels at sample are 12 mW (pump) and 30 mW (Stokes).
Select femtosecond mode by pushing in the knobs on either side of the box.
Select picosecond mode by pulling out the knobs on either side of the box.
Ensure delay stage is correctly positioned for pump and Stokes beams to be temporally overlapped.
Ensure that the dispersion settings of the pump and Stokes beam are correct; set the pump beam to 5 mm and the Stokes beam to 30 mm for an 802 nm pump.
Switch on the signal generator for the beam modulation.
Recall previous settings: OUTPUT 1 as a square wave with Frequency = 19.5 MHz, Amplitude = 1.4 V; OUTPUT 2 as a square wave with Frequency = 19.5 MHz, Amplitude = 300 mV.
Switch on Outputs 1 and 2.
Connect Output 1 to an amplifier for the EOM in the SF-TRU box via a BNC cable.
Connect Output 2 to the lock-in amplifier used for SRS detection via a BNC cable.
Switch on the power supply to the amplifier on the gantry.
Switch on the power supply to the lock-in amplifier on the gantry.
Load the software for the lock-in amplifier “SRS detection Module” on the PC.
In the software, chose Phase = 0°, Offset = -80 mW, Gain = 58 dB.
Select the lock-in amplifier integration time constant in the software: set to 2 µs for cell imaging.
Switch on plugs of all the equipment except the remote-control box.
Wait until standby is lit on the control box located on the top of the gantry.
Switch on the remote-control box on the gantry.
Switch on the back of the remote-control box.
Wait until the remote light turns blue.
Press Start Operation.
Turn on the PC of the laser scanning microscope.
Run the confocal microscope software.
Check the light path of the microscope via the computer software.
Select a 775 nm short pass in the Lightpath tab for SRS imaging.
Connect CARS signal from the PMT to CD1 using a BNC cable.
Connect SRS signal from the lock-in amplifier to CD2 using a BNC cable.
Control the focus through the touch screen or remote-control knobs or computer software.
Select desired image settings in the software, including zoom and pixel dwell time.
Ensure imaging speed is greater than integration time set in the lock-in amplifier software.
Culture 4T1 mouse mammary carcinoma cells in RPMI-1640 supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS).
Change the medium every 2 days.
Passage the cells at 70%-80% confluence.
Incubate 1 x 10^5 cells on square coverslips for 24 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Wash the cells with pre-warmed phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the cells with gold nanoparticles in a 1:100 dilution in cell culture medium for 4 h.
Prior to imaging, wash the cells with ice-cold PBS.
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 15 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash the cells with PBS three times.
Mount the cells between two coverslips for imaging.
Place a droplet of distilled water on top of the water immersion objective focusing the laser beams into the sample between the objective and the sample.
Place the sample on the microscope stage.
Apply a droplet of water between the condenser and the sample for imaging.
Adjust the height of the condenser to approximately 1 mm above the sample.
Move the SRS detector out of the beam path.
Place the detector back into the beam path for SRS imaging.
Select 802 nm wavelength for laser to image CH vibrations between 2,800–3,100 cm-1.
Adjust laser wavelength via software for amide I peak at 1,600 cm-1 by selecting pump beam at 898 nm.
Perform small adjustments in Raman shift by scanning the delay stage in the SF-TRU unit.
Conduct calibration hyperspectral scan using polystyrene beads to determine linear equation converting delay stage position from mm to Raman shift in cm-1.
Generate a hyperspectral scan by taking a time series of images at different delay stage positions.
Use the analog unit to send a TTL signal from TRIG OUT VD1 to the SF-TRU system to move the delay stage +1 increment.
Receive a signal via TRIG In 1 when the delay stage has finished its movement and use this signal to trigger the next image in the time series.
In the Trigger tab of the confocal microscope software, select Start by TTL trigger (ON) and Trigger (every frame).
Set the time series ON and the z series OFF in the Series tab.
Set the number of frames in the time series to match the number of steps in the ATM software.
Go to the Run tab in the ATM software.
Set the delay stage positions in millimeters for the start and stop of the hyperspectral scan.
Use a start position = 90.25 mm and a stop position = 92.25 mm for the CH high wavenumber region.
Ensure that the number of steps matches the number of frames in the confocal microscope software.
Start the hyperspectral stack in the confocal microscope software.
Click on Start Scan under Acquire.
In the ATM software, click on Start to begin image collection.
Export the hyperspectral image series as a multi-frame .tif file.
Use suitable software to carry out calibration of images.
Convert the delay stage position to Raman shifts using the linear calibration equation.
Change the pump wavelength in the laser software from 802 nm to 898 nm for imaging in the amide I vibrational region.
Adjust the Stokes dispersion setting in the ATM software from 30 mm to 5 mm.
Make a small adjustment to the mirror in the pump beam dispersion pathway inside the SF-TRU box by adjusting the lower knob on the mirror mount.
Set the start and stop positions in the ATM software to 89 and 91mm, respectively for scanning over the amide I region.
Wear laser safety goggles when performing steps involving exposure of the laser beam.
